ground_truth.modified_snippet: The option used in G*Power was 'ANOVA: Repeated measures, within-between'.

matched_finding.subcategory: Underpowered interaction test relative to stated sample
matched_finding.description: The authors state that for a medium effect (Cohen f = 0.25) the required sample size for the general interaction is 112 participants, and for planned pairwise comparisons it is 82. With a planned N of 240, the study appears adequately powered for medium effects. However, the correlation between repeated measures used in the interaction power analysis (r = 0.07) is extremely low, which inflates the required sample size. If the true correlation is higher (which is plausible for memory items), the required N would be lower and the study would be overpowered for medium effects. Conversely, if the true effect of the interventions is small (f = 0.10), the study is severely underpowered (required N = 664 vs. planned N = 240). The authors acknowledge this but do not adequately discuss the implications for interpreting null results for the intervention effects.
matched_finding.quote: For the general interaction, that is, between the grouping factor with four groups and the within-subjects factor, the required sample sizes for the small, medium, and large effects were 664, 112, and 48 participants, respectively... Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Counterbalancing removed — must know item confounds are fatal for within-subjects discussed/not-discussed comparison
ground_truth.original_snippet: In order to counterbalance the discussed details, 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs. For example, half the pairs will talk about Eric's cap color but without discussing his company logo (version A of the discussion), while the other pairs will d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.
ground_truth.description: Removed item counterbalancing — without it, discussed vs non-discussed comparison confounds item difficulty with experimental manipulation

matched_finding.description: The authors state that 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase,' meaning all pairs discuss identical items. This eliminates item-level variability in the misinformation exposure but also means that the 'discussed' vs. 'non-discussed' within-subjects comparison is confounded with item identity: the same four items are always in the 'discussed' condition and the same four are always in the 'non-discussed' condition. Although the authors mention that 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced,' this appears to contradict the statement that all pairs discuss the same four details. This inconsistency needs clarification, as true counterbalancing of which items are discussed vs. not discussed is essential for valid within-subjects comparisons.
matched_finding.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase... In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Disputed/non-disputed classification removed — must know not all discussed items contain misinformation
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize participants’ answers into two groups: "disputed" and "non-disputed". More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s ...
ground_truth.description: Removed disputed/non-disputed classification — treats all discussed items as containing misinformation when some may not have; conflates delivered vs non-delivered misinformation

matched_finding.description: The authors state that 'all discussed items' will be categorized as having contained misinformation, regardless of whether the partner actually provided misinformation during the discussion. The analysis plan states: 'while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.' However, the procedure also states that 'if the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented,' implying that some discussions may not result in misinformation being accepted or even clearly delivered. Treating all discussed items as misinformation items regardless of actual discussion content misclassifies items and introduces measurement error.
matched_finding.quote: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

ground_truth.original_snippet: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation after the collaborative recall phase (that is, after exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to make our research closer to real life settings. In reality, one rarely has a chance to do...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take eff...
ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.description: The authors state they decided to place the interventions before the individual memory test but after the collaborative recall (misinformation exposure). This means participants have already been exposed to misinformation before receiving any protective intervention. The authors justify this by saying they 'wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect,' but this is internally contradictory: the misinformation has already been delivered during the collaborative recall phase before the interventions are applied. The interventions are therefore post-exposure warnings, not true inoculations. The authors' own rationale for pre-exposure placement is undermined by the actual procedure.
matched_finding.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect.

If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size. We realize that this may ...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.
ground_truth.description: Removed pre-registered exclusion of hypothesis-aware participants — critical safeguard in deception paradigm; also removed acknowledgment of differential exclusion risk

matched_finding.description: The exclusion criteria section states only that 'we will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.' No other exclusion criteria are specified, such as: participants who guess the study's true purpose (hypothesis awareness), participants who fail attention checks, participants who report prior knowledge of the MORI technique or DRM paradigm, participants with color vision deficiencies (relevant for the polarized glasses), or participants who do not complete all phases. The absence of pre-specified exclusion criteria creates substantial analytic flexibility and risks post-hoc exclusions that could bias results.
matched_finding.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Within-pair age matching removed — must know authority dynamics in memory conformity
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.
ground_truth.description: Removed within-pair age matching — age differences activate authority/deference dynamics that inflate conformity through social influence rather than informational influence

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Completely ruled out' vs 'has little use' — must recognize experimenter-awareness caveat was theoretically important
ground_truth.original_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the p...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'has little use' to 'completely ruled out' and removed experimenter-awareness caveat — overclaims mechanism specificity

matched_finding.subcategory: Contradiction between normative influence exclusion and study design
matched_finding.description: The authors claim that 'the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.' However, the collaborative recall phase involves face-to-face discussion between pairs, during which normative influence (social pressure to agree) is entirely possible and likely. The authors appear to be referring only to the individual memory test phase, but normative influence during the discussion phase could affect memory encoding and retrieval, which would then manifest in the individual test. The blanket exclusion of normative influence as a mechanism is therefore unjustified.
matched_finding.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The Analysis Plan states 'the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format,' but the Methods section states 'The test will contain 20 open-ended questions.' These are mutually contradictory formats. Open-ended questions and two-alternative forced-choice questions are fundamentally different response formats with different scoring procedures, different susceptibility to guessing, and different statistical properties. The manuscript cannot be both simultaneously, and this inconsistency makes it impossible to evaluate the study's measurement approach.
matched_finding.quote: Methods: 'The test will contain 20 open-ended questions' vs. Analysis Plan: 'the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format'

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
